summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a complex history of fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstructions, and G-tube dependence, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging showed no acute obstruction but revealed adhesions causing dilation of the duodenum and proximal jejunum. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube suction, and IV pain control. TPN was initiated due to chronic malnutrition and continued at home. She developed a port-a-cath-associated coagulase-negative staph bacteremia, treated with two weeks of IV vancomycin and lock therapy, with negative follow-up cultures. Her G-tube was replaced twice during the stay due to leakage and accidental dislodgement. Due to subtherapeutic INR unresponsive to warfarin escalation, she was transitioned to enoxaparin for anticoagulation. She was discharged home with TPN, home health services, and plans for outpatient follow-up, including surveillance blood cultures.
